John — thanks, great to hear the commercial package is acceptable. Quick plan from our side: 

- Signing order (DocuSign): 1) StapleTech primary signer (John/Marta) -> 2) Redwood CFO (Ben Carter) -> 3) Redwood Legal (Rachel Kim) for final countersignature. That ensures StapleTech signs first and our systems auto-verify before we apply the company seal.
- Signer authority: we will include a short signer-authority cover sheet in the envelope requesting that StapleTech attach the signer’s title + POA document (if signing on behalf of a subsidiary). If you prefer, Marta can upload the POA ahead of time and we’ll preload it into the envelope.
- Notary/witness: Redwood can accommodate an additional recipient step (offline notarization) — after StapleTech signs we will pause the envelope and await a flattened, notarized PDF from your side if required, then complete the envelope after we receive it. That keeps the DocuSign audit trail intact while meeting your notary needs.
- Final artifacts: once fully executed we will: a) publish a flattened, stamped PDF to the DocuSign envelope and b) push the clean copy to the HubSpot deal and to the S3 exec bucket for your records (we’ll also share a signed PDF copy via the DocuSign link).

Attachments: Redlined_MSA_v7.pdf (final clean), OrderForm_StapleTech_20260810.pdf (attached in envelope).

Rachel — can you confirm this satisfies our internal signature sequencing and whether we should require a notarization recipient step for outbound envelopes in this region?
Ben — please confirm CFO availability for a countersignature window tomorrow afternoon (PDT).

Thanks — Soojin
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
